[[Cancún Challenge]] champions |bowl=[[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result=Sweet Sixteen }} {{2016–17 Big Ten men's basketball standings}} The '''2016–17 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team''' represented [[Purdue University]] in the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. Their head coach was [[Matt Painter]], in his 12th season with the Boilers. The team played their home games in [[Mackey Arena]] in [[West Lafayette, Indiana]] and were members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. With their win over [[2016–17 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]] on February 28, 2017, Purdue clinched their first Big Ten Championship since 2009, 22nd overall.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400914990|title=Indiana vs. Purdue - Game Recap - February 28, 2017 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-03-03}} With [[2016–17 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]]'s loss on March 2, Purdue clinched an outright championship, their 23rd championship, the most in Big Ten history.{{Cite news|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030217aaa.html|title=Purdue Men's Basketball Clinches Outright Big Ten Championship|access-date=2017-03-03|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170320004827/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030217aaa.html|archive-date=2017-03-20|url-status=dead}} They finished the season 27–8, 14–4 in to win the [[2016–17 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten regular season championship]]. In the [[2017 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they lost in the quarterfinals to [[2016–17 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 4 seed in the Midwest Region where they beat [[2016–17 Vermont Catamounts men's basketball team|Vermont]] and [[2016–17 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]] to advance to the Sweet Sixteen. In their first trip to the Sweet Sixteen since [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2010]], they lost to No. 1-seeded and No. 3-ranked [[2016–17 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]]. ==Previous season== The [[2015–16 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Boilermakers]] finished the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16 season]] with a record of 26–9, 12–6 in [[2015–16 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a four-way tie for third place. As the No. 4 seed in the [[2016 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2015–16 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] and [[2015–16 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] to advance to the championship game. In the championship game, they lost to [[2015–16 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]]. The Boilermakers received an at-large bid to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where, as a No. 5 seed, they were upset by No. 12-seeded [[2015–16 Little Rock Trojans men's basketball team|Little Rock]] in the first round. ==Preseason== Purdue was picked to finish second in the Big Ten in preseason polls by [[Sports Illustrated]]{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2016/10/24/big-ten-preview-wisconsin-purdue-indiana|title=Wisconsin's experience makes it a Big Ten favorite|last=Winn|first=Luke|newspaper=SI.com|access-date=2017-02-10}} and [[USA Today]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/bigten/2016/10/24/big-ten-conference-college-basketball-rankings-2016-17-season-preview/92680128/|title=Big Ten Conference college basketball season preview for 2016-17|newspaper=USA TODAY|access-date=2017-02-10|language=en}} [[Caleb Swanigan]] was named to the preseason All-Big Ten team as voted by a panel of conference media.{{Cite news|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/101116aaa.html|title=Big Ten Men's Basketball Preseason Honors Announced|access-date=2017-02-10|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161014111857/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/101116aaa.html|archive-date=2016-10-14|url-status=dead}} ==Offseason== ===Departures=== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
